title: Console list page load sends get-session, meta/app, me/permissions and me/apps twice each, concurrently
body:
domain:ui#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbDAucNyQ4UtzCJKyh

Filing gate: ③ ruling-directed. Ruling B on #26676 (6520722066) fixes a new card under #26676 as the remedy for a finding after a landing. Found by the post-merge proxy preview review of PR #27907 (#27626): comment 6522108365, on `main` `18318361`, `examples/app-crm`, 1440×900, evidence branch `claude/issue-27626-proxy-evidence` @ `4c9afa65`. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Business reason
Who: every console reader. What happens: each list page load spends four extra round trips on identical reads. That runs against #27626's Acceptance 1 rule that one URL in flight is fetched once.

## Observed
- On `main`, a list page load sends `auth/get-session`, `meta/app`, `auth/me/permissions` and `me/apps` twice each, at the same time, with identical GETs.
- This is not on the record-open path #27907 changed, so it is not that PR's regression.
- Also seen on the first cold open, as an observation only: `approvals/records/<obj>/<id>/lock` answers 501 and logs a console error. Measure whether that route is expected to be absent in `app-crm`.

## Wanted
Each of the four reads is made once per load, and a second caller shares the in-flight request.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A list page load makes one request per URL for the four reads. Pinned by a request-count test, with an ablation.
